tweets.text:
How Primus Turns Encrypted State into Auditable Institutional Privacy

Institutions on public chains face a basic problem either show every position and strategy, or hide everything and lose the ability to operate or satisfy auditors.

@primus_labs addresses this with Fully Homomorphic Encryption that keeps balances and amounts encrypted Onchain while smart contracts still update them. The numbers stay hidden by default.

Encryption alone is not the full answer. There must also be a controlled way to open a specific value later. Primus describes the encrypted data as a sealed envelope that can be processed without being opened. Contents remain private unless access to a particular value is authorized and recorded.

An access control layer sits on top of this encrypted state so decryption becomes an explicit, logged exception rather than the normal case. Auditors or regulators can check what is needed when properly authorized, while the rest of the market never sees the strategy.

The design aims to give real capital both operational privacy and a verifiable trail.

tweets.text:
If your competitor can see your position size and transfer timing, you are already negotiating from behind.

Public chains gave finance an open settlement layer. Bcz of that, anyone who knows where to look can read your moves too. Exposure changes how other traders react, and it can move the price before your strategy has finished playing out.

Ngl I never understood why this trade off should be permanent. A business can settle on a public chain and still have good reasons to keep its position size private.

That is where the Confidential Finance portal from @primus_labs comes in. You can hold, transfer and earn yield privately on encrypted assets.

Behind it is Primus FHE, which computes directly on encrypted data. Only the authorized data owner can decrypt the result

My view is simple. Confidentiality has to work during computation, not just while data sits in storage. Encrypt an asset and then expose it every time you use it, and the hard part is still unsolved

Btw Primus also pairs FHE with GPU acceleration to balance performance and cost. Speed and cost will decide whether private finance gets used outside demos

Join Primus with me here 👇

tweets.text:
Good morning everyone! ☀️

One of the biggest barriers preventing institutions from fully embracing DeFi is not the technology itself, but financial privacy.

On a public blockchain, every transaction can be tracked. For institutions managing significant capital, exposing balances and transaction details is a serious concern.
This is exactly the problem @primus_labs is working to address.

One interesting example is the Confidential Vault on BNB Chain.

Users can convert U-tokens into encrypted eU-tokens, transfer them, and deploy them into yield-generating strategies while keeping sensitive financial information private. When needed, they can convert them back.

What makes this approach interesting is that it brings privacy into an environment that remains publicly verifiable.

Behind this vision are several technologies working together:

→ FHE: Enables smart contracts to process encrypted data without revealing sensitive information.
→ zkTLS + TEE + zkVM: Help establish trust in external data and support verifiable financial claims, including Proof of Reserves.

Primus is also moving beyond technology development through collaborations with Unitas and UnitedStables, exploring how privacy-preserving infrastructure can support real DeFi use cases.

I believe this direction could be important for the next stage of blockchain adoption.

Institutions need privacy, but the ecosystem still needs ways to verify that assets and financial claims are legitimate.

The challenge is finding the right balance between these two requirements.

Of course, scalability, processing costs, user experience and regulatory compliance still need to be proven in practice.

But the idea is worth paying attention to:

What if we could verify financial information without having to reveal it?
That's the future @primus_labs is trying to build.

Privacy shouldn't be a barrier to transparency. With the right infrastructure, both can coexist onchain. 🐧
